analysis.title: Ford Motor Co. (F): 3Q26 First Take
key_insights: GS calls Ford's 3Q26 a mixed report: revenue and adjusted EBIT beat the Street (FactSet) and the full-year EBIT guidance midpoint was raised, but the implied 4Q26 EBIT guide midpoint is below both GS and the Street.
GS assumes higher commodity costs contribute to the lower 4Q guide, since the 2026 commodity headwind was raised to approaching ~$2.5 bn from just above $2 bn.
GS expects the call to focus on what the 4Q EBIT trajectory implies for 2027 EBIT.

Other expected call topics: truck outlook including recovery after Novelis-related supply challenges, commodity and logistics costs, warranty, software & services growth, and demand traction in Ford Energy.
3Q26 total company revenue was $49.5 bn vs GS $51.1 bn and Street $49.1 bn. Total wholesale units were 1,049k vs GS 1,103k.
3Q26 adjusted EBIT was $2.7 bn (5.4% of sales) vs GS $2.3 bn (4.4%) and Street $2.4 bn (5.0%). Non-GAAP operating EPS was $0.49 vs GS $0.38 and Street $0.41. Adjusted FCF was $4.7 bn.

Ford attributed the y/y EBIT increase to better volume/mix (~$0.2 bn), pricing (~$0.1 bn), and lower regulatory expenses plus higher software and services contributions (~$0.4 bn), partly offset by ~$0.7 bn of higher costs.

Ford raised the low end of CY26 EBIT guidance to $10.5-$11.0 bn from $10.0-$11.0 bn (GS $10.7 bn, Street $10.6 bn), citing operational execution and strength in Ford Credit and Software, Services, and Parts.
Guidance now assumes US industry pricing up ~1.0% y/y (from ~0.5%) and a US SAAR of 16.5 mn (from 16.0-16.5 mn). It excludes impacts from a sustained Middle East conflict or a US economic downturn.

Segment guidance: Ford Blue EBIT ~$5.5 bn (from $5.0-$5.5 bn), Ford Pro ~$7.0 bn (from $7.0-$7.5 bn), Model e about -$4.0 bn (unchanged), Ford Credit EBT ~$2.8 bn (from >$2.5 bn). CY26 adjusted FCF of $6.0-$7.0 bn and capex of $9.5-$10.5 bn are unchanged.
Implied 4Q26 adjusted EBIT guide is about $2.1 bn at the midpoint vs GS $2.4 bn and Street $2.2 bn.
Per Reuters and CNBC, Ford expects 2027 profitability roughly in line with 2026, partly citing rising commodity costs, implying EBIT of ~$10.75 bn vs Street $11.25 bn and GS $11.27 bn.
GS keeps a Neutral rating and $14 12-month price target on F (7X normalized EPS of $2.05); the stock closed at $11.95 on 28 Oct 2026.

market_movers.rationale: GS keeps Neutral and a $14 target (7X normalized EPS of $2.05), 17.2% above the $11.95 price. Revenue and EBIT beat, but the implied 4Q26 EBIT guide and 2027 profit outlook sit below GS and Street.

earnings_insights: Ford 3Q26 reported total company revenue $49.5 bn vs GS est $51.1 bn and Street (FactSet) est $49.1 bn.
Ford 3Q26 reported adjusted EBIT $2.7 bn (5.4% of sales) vs GS est $2.3 bn (4.4%) and Street est $2.4 bn (5.0%).
Ford 3Q26 reported non-GAAP operating EPS $0.49 vs GS est $0.38 and Street est $0.41. Adjusted FCF reported at $4.7 bn.
3Q26 wholesale units reported at 1,049k vs GS est 1,103k (-4.9%), down 9.3% y/y. By segment: Ford Blue 657k, Model e 34k, Ford Pro 358k.
3Q26 segment EBIT reported: Ford Blue $1,392 mn (5.1% margin), Model e -$1,058 mn, Ford Pro $1,665 mn (9.4% margin), Ford Credit EBT $803 mn.
GS estimates 3Q26 ASPs: Ford Blue ~$46.2k (-1% q/q, +6% y/y), Model e ~$36.0k (-2% q/q, +1% y/y), Ford Pro ~$51.8k (+3% q/q, +4% y/y).
Ford CY26 adjusted EBIT guidance is $10.5-$11.0 bn (midpoint $10.75 bn) vs GS est $10.7 bn and Street est $10.6 bn. Commodity headwind now approaching ~$2.5 bn (from just above $2 bn).
Implied 4Q26 adjusted EBIT guidance midpoint is ~$2.1 bn (range $1.85-$2.35 bn) vs GS est $2.4 bn and Street est $2.2 bn, 12.5% below GS and 4.7% below Street.
Implied 4Q26 segment EBIT guide: Ford Blue ~$1,031 mn, Model e ~-$1,246 mn, Ford Pro ~$1,932 mn, Ford Credit EBT ~$457 mn.
2027 EBIT implied at ~$10.75 bn per Reuters/CNBC reporting of Ford's comments, vs Street est $11.25 bn and GS est $11.27 bn.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Ford's raised guidance assumption for total US SAAR, from 16.0-16.5 mn previously.
Ford's guidance assumption, raised from up ~0.5% y/y, supporting the higher full-year EBIT low end.

risk_factors: Higher commodity costs: 2026 headwind raised to approaching ~$2.5 bn and cited as pressure on 2027 profitability.
A sustained Middle East conflict or US economic downturn, both excluded from guidance.
Auto cycle risk: demand and price-mix could be weaker or stronger than GS expects.
Market share gains or losses at Ford, and tariff impact larger or smaller than expected.
Margin pressure in a downturn, execution on the hybrid/EV transition, and ability to grow higher-margin software & services.
Model e continues to lose money (guided EBIT about -$4.0 bn for 2026).
Truck supply recovery after Novelis-related supply challenges.
geopolitical: Ford's 2026 guidance excludes potential impacts from a sustained Middle East conflict.

tension_points.bull_case: Ford beat 3Q26 revenue and EBIT, raised the low end of 2026 EBIT guidance to $10.5-$11.0 bn, and cited strength in Ford Credit and Software, Services, and Parts.
tension_points.bear_case: The implied 4Q26 EBIT midpoint of ~$2.1 bn is below GS ($2.4 bn) and the Street ($2.2 bn), and rising commodity costs imply 2027 EBIT of ~$10.75 bn vs Street $11.25 bn.
tension_points.what_invalidates: The 4Q EBIT trajectory and what it implies for 2027 EBIT, which GS expects to be a key focus on the call.
